outcome: Apgar scores at 5 mins below 7 points
cohort: The study enrolled 337 full-term primigravida with uncomplicated singleton pregnancies who underwent transabdominal ultrasound between 37(+0) and 41(+0) weeks of gestation.
finding: Abnormal umbilical coiling (both hypo- and hypercoiling) was significantly associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes including fetal growth restriction (7-fold risk), Apgar scores at 5 minutes < 7 points (8-fold risk), meconium-stained amniotic fluid, cesarean delivery, and birth weight below 2500 grams.
mod_finding: Abnormal umbilical coiling was associated with a significantly higher rate of cesarean delivery compared to normocoiling.
cross-section timing: Antenatal, between 37(+0) and 41(+0) weeks of gestation, with monitoring until birth delivery.
